ai.title: Add minimal change instruction to main prompt
ai.summary: Injected <additional_instruction> block into mainPrompt to enforce minimal code changes. Backend/src/main-prompt.ts modified. Directs agent to complete core request and pause for instructions.

eli5.text: The assistant will now make smaller, more focused changes instead of rewriting whole sections, and it will stop and ask you before doing extra work. You may notice it proposing shorter edits that stick closely to what you asked. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment to how it decides the scope of its changes.

ai.title: Bump manicode to 1.0.43
ai.summary: Version bumped from 1.0.42 to 1.0.43 in `backend/package.json` and `npm-app/package.json`. CLI undo/redo output messages updated in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to use present tense. Added known issues and testing notes to `todo.knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: The assistant's undo and redo commands now say 'Undo' and 'Redo' instead of 'Undoing' and 'Redoing'. This is a minor behind-the-scenes update to the assistant's version number, and you would only notice the slightly shorter wording in the command output.

ai.title: System prompt: file context, uncertainty pause, two-fail stop
ai.summary: getSystemPrompt injects <files> list from truncatedFiles keys and requires explicit 'I have all the files I need' confirmation before proceeding. High uncertainty (>5) now mandates pausing without file modification. Step 4 adds a hard stop after two consecutive command/task failures, requiring user guidance. Knowledge file rules expanded with concrete examples (package managers, function choices, style, tests).

eli5.text: The assistant now reads a list of files you've provided and must explicitly confirm it has everything it needs before making changes. If the task feels uncertain or ambiguous, it pauses instead of guessing and editing. It also stops after a second failed attempt (like running a command or test that broke twice) and asks how to proceed. These are guardrails so the assistant is more careful and transparent, and they are live today.

ai.title: Refactor system prompt into modular pieces
ai.summary: Refactored `getSystemPrompt` in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to compose the prompt from distinct constants and helper functions (`introPrompt`, `getProjectFilesPrompt`, `editingFilesPrompt`, `getKnowledgeFilesPrompt`, `getToolsPrompt`, `getResponseFormatPrompt`). This improves readability and maintainability of the core prompt logic. No user-visible behavior changes.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions were split into labeled sections instead of being one long block, making them easier to read and update. You won't notice any difference in how the assistant behaves; it still gives the same answers and makes the same kinds of suggestions as before.

ai.title: Restructure backend system prompt
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts reorders and splits prompt sections. getProjectFilesPrompt replaced by getProjectFileTreePrompt and getRelevantFilesPrompt. Knowledge files moved to relevant files block. Tools section reorders run_terminal_command before web_scrape. Intro prompt consolidates project access details.

eli5.text: Internally, the assistant's instructions were reorganized so that project-file information is now split into two clearer sections: one listing the overall project layout, and another listing only the specific files relevant to the current task. Knowledge files are now grouped together near these file sections, and the list of available tools now shows the terminal command tool before the web-scraping tool. If you looked at the assistant's setup, you would see these sections appearing in a different order and with the old combined file listing replaced by the two separate ones. This is live today as an internal change to how the assistant receives its instructions.

ai.title: Anthropic prompt caching for system prompt prefix
ai.summary: Added `anthropic-beta: prompt-caching-2024-07-31` header and `cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }` to the first system prompt block in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. The prompt is now an array of two text blocks: the first contains static instructions, file tree, and knowledge files; the second contains dynamic relevant files and response format. This split allows the stable prefix to be cached across requests, reducing latency and token usage for the knowledge files and file tree sections.

eli5.text: The assistant now saves the project's file list and coding rules in a temporary memory slot between requests, so follow-up questions reuse that context instead of resending it every time. This makes second and later questions to the same project load faster and cost less to run. You won't see a new menu or button, but conversations with the assistant on larger projects should feel a bit snappier and more consistent.

ai.title: Defer CLI setup to first message
ai.summary: CLI startup no longer blocks on `initFingerprint`, `getProjectFileContext`, or `client.connect`. `index.ts` aggregates these into a `readyPromise` passed to the `CLI` constructor. `cli.ts` awaits this promise only when submitting a user message, allowing the terminal prompt to appear instantly. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/cli.ts` and `npm-app/src/index.ts`.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant in your terminal, the window now shows its prompt and lets you start typing right away instead of making you wait while it loads up. The assistant now finishes all of its behind-the-scenes setup work only after you've already sent in your first question, so the initial delay you used to see is gone. This makes the terminal feel instantly responsive the moment you open it. If you looked at the code, you'd see the startup work and the message handling were rearranged so the prompt appears before any of the setup finishes.

ai.title: Cache project file context
ai.summary: Added caching for `getProjectFileContext` in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`. File tree and knowledge files are computed once per session and reused, while only `files` are refreshed. `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` notes this caching behavior.

eli5.text: When you start a conversation with the assistant, it reads your project's file list and knowledge files once, then remembers that information for the rest of the session instead of re-reading them every time you ask a question. You wouldn't notice this directly, but the assistant will respond faster and won't repeatedly reload the same project details during your conversation. This only applies to the file tree and knowledge files, which stay cached, while individual file contents are still refreshed as needed.

ai.title: Improve websocket error handling and startup logs
ai.summary: WebSocket client now suppresses repeated error logs during reconnect attempts, printing 'Could not connect. Retrying...' once and 'Reconnected!' on success. CLI startup logs and git directory checks moved to occur after client initialization completes. Affects `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts` and `npm-app/src/index.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant loses its live connection to the server and needs to retry, you will now see a single quiet 'Could not connect. Retrying...' line instead of the same error repeating over and over, followed by a small 'Reconnected!' confirmation once it is back. That retry notice and the green success message will not appear anywhere else in the startup sequence. You may also see the assistant's welcome message and the check for your project's version-control folder arrive a moment later than before, after its main connection is ready.
